answer.rationale: The degradation is confined to the primary region with write-path p99 at 5x target during peak settlement traffic, which matches the memory_b2 pattern (regional failover restored latency in minutes with clean traffic shift). Rollback is off the table due to the compliance-mandated security patch, so memory_b1/b6 don't apply. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) targets read load, but this is a write-path problem. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) fit a partner dependency outage, not a regional primary degradation. Add capacity is the fallback if verification of memory_b2 surfaces conditions that don't hold now (e.g., cause being the new release rather than regional infrastructure). Failover risk to in-flight writes is real at settlement peak, so I flag downstream value risk and hold capacity-adding as the queued second option.
